title: Little Black Joe and Joe Lindsey, drummers father taught
summary: Father taught young drummers who worked in his shop and subbed for him: Little Black Joe and Joe Lindsey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did your father ever give any music lessons or teach any other drummers or anybody that you ever saw around the house? Yeah, he did.

I can tell you one boy I remember that was a fine little drummer that my daddy taught. He worked for my daddy. And my daddy, we used to call him Joe. Little Black Joe. He was a little dog fella in the car. He worked for my father for years in the shop.
You don't remember his last name? No, I don't remember his name. I know they used to call him Joe.
Little Black Joe. Because many nights, when my father didn't play on the job, he'd send him. And he'd play in his place, but they called him Joe.
No, I know Joe Lindsey well.
He worked with my daddy. He was around my daddy when my daddy was playing drums, Joe Lindsey. I know him well. You've seen him lately.
He died about, oh, five or six years ago. Yeah.
I didn't know Joe Lindsey had died.
About five or six at least. Maybe a little bit.

I remember him well then. He was a fella a little older than I am. Yeah. But he'd come up over me. But he played drum around my dad too. He got a few lessons from my daddy himself. But Joe was the one that my daddy really trained to play, thought to play drum and he was a pretty good drummer. He played several nights he'd go and play in my daddy's place when he didn't want to go out in the cabaret. He'd go take his place. Well I remember that boy he taught music but anybody else I don't remember.
